sections.h2: Where is the Union County Recorder's Office in Marysville?
sections.html:
The Union County Recorder works from the County Office Building at 233 West Sixth Street, Marysville, Ohio 43040. Hours run Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the main number is 937-645-3032. The office describes itself as the official land records office for all real estate in Union County.

Indexing is the core task. Each document is indexed so a searcher can trace a chain of title and see any debt that still attaches to the land. Images and indexes are online from 1995 forward, and the office has recently added grantor and grantee deed indexes from 1875 to 1994, mortgage indexes from 1944 to 1994 and miscellaneous indexes from 1960 to 1994. For older papers that are not digitized, staff can send copies by email, fax or mail.

The same building holds the county auditor and treasurer, so a seller handling a deed, a tax question and a recording can finish all three in one visit.

sections.h2: What does the Union County Recorder charge in fees?
sections.html:
Fees rose by $5 on January 1, 2025, after Senate Bill 94 allowed a document preservation surcharge under Ohio Revised Code 317.32. The county's fee chart sets deeds, mortgages, affidavits, easements, leases, land contracts and powers of attorney at $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after that.

Union County Recorder fees from the county fee schedule
ServiceFee
Deed, mortgage or similar document, first two pages$39
Each added page$8
Marginal reference on a separate instrument$4 each, on top of the recording fee
Copy, per page$2
Certified copy$1 per document added to the copy fee
Document that is not conforming$20
Veterans' discharge papersNo fee

Source: Union County Recorder fee schedule.

The county's one-to-ten page chart prints $39 for one or two pages, $47 for three, $63 for five and $103 for ten. Plats and condominium drawings are priced at ten cents per square inch, and the county asks for an 18 by 24 inch sheet. Zoning resolutions are $50 and zoning amendments $20.

sections.h2: How does a Union County deed get to the recorder?
sections.html:
The Union County Recorder takes conveyances by mail only when the Auditor's conveyance stamp is already on the document. That points to the usual order in this county: the deed goes to the Auditor first, then to the Recorder.

  • The grantee or a representative files the statement of value under section 319.202, which the county provides as form DTE 100. An exempt transfer uses the exemption statement, DTE 100EX.
  • The Auditor collects the conveyance fee, which its conveyance standards page lists at $4 per thousand dollars of value.
  • The Auditor stamps the deed, and the Recorder files it.

The Auditor, Engineer and Recorder adopted a shared set of Real Estate Conveyance Standards on May 1, 2014, after public hearings in February and March of that year. The standards set requirements that the three offices apply to deeds, so ask the title company or attorney to check a draft against them. Some Ohio counties also levy a transfer tax under section 322.02; ask the auditor whether any local charge applies.

Recorders may not accept a document containing a Social Security number unless an affidavit is attached, and the fee schedule cites section 317.082 for that rule. Deed text should be checked before it is submitted.

sections.h2: What layout rules apply to papers filed in Union County?
sections.html:
The county's fee schedule treats a document that misses the state standard in section 317.114 as non-conforming and adds $20. It spells out four points:

  • Print no smaller than 10 point.
  • A 3 inch margin at the top of the first page.
  • A 1 inch margin on each side and the bottom of every page.
  • A 1 1/2 inch margin at the top of the remaining pages.

Have the closing agent check a draft against those four points, since the surcharge applies to each filing that misses them.

sections.h2: Can Union County records be filed or watched online?
sections.html:
Yes, in part. As of July 15, 2024 the office accepts eRecorded filings that are not conveyances. The announcement covers non-conveyance filings, so ask the office how a deed should be submitted.

The office also offers a free real estate fraud alert service for residents. The recorder describes it as a notification service meant to help combat real estate fraud, and the Recorder page links to the sign-up details.

sections.h2: Which liens and releases show up in Union County records?
sections.html:
The fee schedule doubles as a list of the lien types that can attach to a property, which is useful when a title search turns something up. Federal tax liens and federal court judgment abstracts cost $5 to file, and a release of either costs $3. Several state liens are filed with no fee, including workers' compensation liens, Ohio EPA liens, franchise tax liens, personal property tax liens and unemployment compensation liens. A release, partial release or discharge of a franchise tax, personal property tax, tangible or intangible tax, or unemployment compensation lien costs $4.

UCC filings tied to real estate cost $12 plus $4 for each name indexed. Marginal references, the $4 charge that links a release or assignment to the original recorded mortgage, are billed on top of the normal recording fee. A seller with a paid-off mortgage should confirm with the lender that the release was filed, because a mortgage that was never released will still show on the title search.

sections.h2: What is Union County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Union County covers 437 square miles in central Ohio, with Marysville as county seat and largest city. Wikipedia says it was formed in 1820 from parts of Franklin, Delaware, Madison and Logan counties, which gave it its name, and that the present courthouse was dedicated on January 27, 1883. Part of Dublin and part of Plain City lie inside the county, and Richwood, Milford Center, Magnetic Springs and Unionville Center are villages. US 33 runs through Marysville, and Honda's Marysville Auto Plant and Scotts Miracle-Gro are among the large employers.

School districts named for the county include Marysville Exempted Village, Fairbanks, North Union, Triad, Jonathan Alder, Buckeye Valley, Elgin, Benjamin Logan and Dublin City.

The Census Bureau shows a fast-growing market:

  • Population estimate for 2025: 73,446, up 17.0 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024: $344,900.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 79.2 percent among 24,232 households.
  • Median gross rent: $1,247 a month.
  • Median household income: $112,322.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 968.

If your home sits in a platted subdivision, ask the title company to pull the plat and any recorded restrictions along with the deed.

faqs.q: What is the fee to record a deed in Union County, Ohio?
faqs.a: A deed costs $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each added page. Marginal references cost $4 each, and a non-conforming document carries a $20 charge. The Auditor's conveyance fee is paid separately.

faqs.q: Does the Union County Recorder accept deeds by mail?
faqs.a: Only if the Union County Auditor's conveyance stamp is already on the document. The fee schedule states this rule, so send the deed to the Auditor first and then mail the stamped original with the correct fee.

faqs.q: What are the Union County Recorder's office hours?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. at 233 West Sixth Street in Marysville. The phone number is 937-645-3032.

faqs.q: Can I eRecord a deed in Union County?
faqs.a: The recorder began accepting eRecorded non-conveyance filings on July 15, 2024. For a deed, ask the office how to submit, since the Auditor's conveyance stamp has to be on it first.

faqs.q: What does the Union County Auditor charge to transfer a deed?
faqs.a: The county's conveyance standards page lists a conveyance fee of $4 per thousand dollars of value. Ask the Auditor's office for any per-parcel charge and whether a local transfer tax applies to your deed.
